summary: A Java JSON web service on Quarkus and Maven with one error format, request logs, readiness checks and null checks at compile time.
description: Write a Java HTTP service on Quarkus with Quarkus REST and Maven. One in-memory notes resource proves the shape: create, read and paged list routes, strict JSON input, and one error envelope for bad input, misses, wrong methods and unexpected failures, all from a single error table. Request ids, JSON access logs, a validated config mapping, readiness and liveness checks and an OpenAPI document come wired. The build formats code, catches nullness bugs and common mistakes at compile time, enforces a coverage floor, checks the layering with ArchUnit and runs the packaged app in its own process for integration tests. It runs on the JVM; a native executable and a database are left for the project to add.
seoDescription: A Quarkus REST API recipe in Java with Maven, one JSON error envelope, request ids and logs, SmallRye Health, NullAway and Error Prone, and @QuarkusTest tests.

projectExamples.title: Container-first catalog service
projectExamples.description: Illustrative: replace notes with catalog items that other services read over HTTP, with readiness checks for an orchestrator. Persistence and access control are work the project still has to add.

projectExamples.title: Small event intake endpoint in an image
projectExamples.description: Illustrative: accept events as JSON, validate them and log each request with its id. Storage and delivery are custom work; docker-deploy builds and publishes the image.

plain.whatItIs: A starter web service written in Java on Quarkus, a framework built for containers, that answers requests with JSON data, clear error replies and readiness checks.
goodAt: Backends that run in containers or Kubernetes and must start quickly
Teams that already run Java and want the Quarkus way of doing it
Services that must report every error in one consistent format
notGoodAt: Projects that need a database or sign-in from the start; you add both yourself.
Teams that already standardize on Spring; use the Spring Boot API stack instead.

requests: build a REST API with Quarkus
a Quarkus JSON service built with Maven
Kubernetes-native Java microservice with readiness checks
JAX-RS endpoints on Quarkus with consistent JSON error replies
Java service that starts fast in a container
caveats: Needs a JDK and Maven installed once to create the Maven wrapper; after that the wrapper downloads Maven itself.
Runs in JVM mode; a native executable needs GraalVM or Mandrel and is not set up.
The first build downloads every dependency and plugin, which takes a few minutes.
